newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway union walks out of state-mediated talks.
newsitem.headline: Norway union walks out of state-mediated talks.

text.p: Norway's Trade Union Confederation (LO) walked out on Wednesday of negotiations with management over this year's wage settlements and warned of strike action by 240,000 of its members, the Norwegian NTB news agency said.
The talks between LO and the employers' Confederation of Trade and Industry (NHO) are over retirement age and wage rises.

State appointed mediator Reidar Webster stepped in on Tuesday to try and solve the outstanding issues after initial negotiations collapsed on March 19. He has until midnight (2200 GMT) on Sunday to mediate a deal.
"We have had serious and confident talks on both wage rises and the question of retirement age," was the only comment Webster would make after Wednesday's five-hour session, NTB said.
The parties are due to meet again on Friday.
NHO says last year's nationwide talks meant real term wage growth of nearly three percent, helping to fuel inflation and hurting the competitiveness of Norwegian export industry.
A series of strikes hurting the offshore and manufacturing industries marred Norway's labour scene for a few months last year after state-led mediation failed to bring parties together in time.
